name: Legends of Huaxia
period: the age of the Three Sovereigns
desc: The ancestors of Chinese legend: Suiren who drilled the first fire, Fuxi who knotted the first nets, Shennong who tasted a hundred herbs. Their gifts and their tales are the tribe's own.
source: Han-era collections of older myths: Huainanzi, Shiji, the Xici commentary of the Yi Jing

devout: counted the moons on a knotted cord through a whole winter
gluttonous: tasted a bitter root that every elder warned against, and lived

inventions.name: Knotted Fishing Net
inventions.source: Yi Jing, Xici commentary: Fuxi knotted cords into nets for hunting and fishing
inventions.desc: Cords knotted into nets, as Fuxi taught: fishing yields 30% more.
inventions.hint: Needs a fishing ground, and hunters with time to knot cords.

inventions.name: Leisi Digging Plough
inventions.source: Yi Jing, Xici commentary: Shennong bent wood into the lei and si
inventions.desc: A forked wooden spade, as Shennong made: farm plots yield 25% more.
inventions.hint: Needs farming, and many days of working the soil.

inventions.name: Knotted Cords
inventions.source: Yi Jing, Xici commentary: in high antiquity they governed by knotted cords
inventions.desc: Knots on a cord keep count of moons, debts and deeds: the tribe gathers a little more lore.
inventions.hint: Comes from leading others and keeping the rites.

inventions.name: Silk Reeling
inventions.source: Later legend credits Leizu, wife of the Yellow Emperor; a cut silkworm cocoon was found at the Yangshao site of Xiyincun
inventions.desc: Threads unwound from the cocoons of the mulberry worm: +3 mood, and the cold bites a little less.
inventions.hint: Needs wild mulberries and the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and long evenings of patient hands.

foods.name: Shennong's Herb Broth
foods.source: Huainanzi: Shennong tasted the hundred plants, meeting seventy poisons in a day
foods.desc: Roots and leaves simmered by one who has tasted them all: the sick recover 15% faster, the hurt heal 10% faster.
foods.hint: Needs willow bark, and someone who forages and keeps the rites.

foods.name: Millet Wine
foods.source: Zhanguo Ce: Yi Di made wine and offered it to Yu; residues of fermented drink are known from Jiahu (c. 7000 BCE)
foods.desc: Grain left to sour in a sealed jar turns sweet and strong: +4 mood, and rites bring 10% more devotion.
foods.hint: Needs pottery and farming, and grain kept by the fire.

finds.name: Wild Mulberry
finds.desc: Dark sweet berries; pale worms spin their cocoons on the leaves.

finds.name: Five-Coloured Stones
finds.source: Huainanzi: Nüwa smelted stones of five colours to patch the sky
finds.desc: Pebbles of red, yellow, green, white and black. Each load is lore, and rites bring 10% more devotion once they are known.

people.name: Suiren
people.desc: Who first twirled a stick in dry wood until it smoked, and gave the people cooked food.

people.name: Youchao
people.desc: Who taught the people to raise shelters of branches in the trees, safe from beasts.

people.name: Fuxi
people.desc: Who knotted the first nets, tamed beasts and drew the eight trigrams from the marks of earth and sky.

people.name: Nüwa
people.desc: Who shaped the first people from yellow clay, and mended the broken sky.

people.name: Shennong
people.desc: Who tasted a hundred plants to learn which heal and which kill, and taught the people to sow.

people.name: Cangjie
people.desc: Who looked at the tracks of birds and beasts and made the first written signs.

people.name: Yi Di
people.text: a stranger with a sealed jar on her back, who says grain can be made to sing.
memory: brewed a wine so strong that the great Yu swore off it
people.desc: The legendary first maker of wine, who offered it to Yu the Great.

people.name: Yu
people.label: Yu the Flood-Tamer
people.desc: A builder of levees and canals. Crafting 7, Lore 5.

people.name: Chiyou
people.label: Chiyou the Berserker
people.desc: A storm of bronze and fury. Combat 8, 90 HP.

events.title: Ten Suns in the Sky
events.source: Huainanzi: in the time of Yao ten suns rose together and scorched the crops
events.text: The drought will not break. The children say they have counted ten suns in the white sky, and the old say the same happened long ago, until an archer shot nine of them down.

options.label: Offer to the sun-mother Xihe
options.result: Smoke rises from the offering all day. That night the tribe dreams of a single, gentle sun.

options.label: Let the archers shoot at the sky

do.remember: shot arrows at the burning sky in the time of drought

options.result: Arrows fly at the noon sky until arms ache. Nothing falls, but no one feels helpless any more.

options.label: Wait in the shade
options.result: The tribe lies in the shade and waits, thirsty and sullen.

events.title: Tracks in the Mud
events.source: Xunzi and Huainanzi: Cangjie made writing; when he did, grain rained from the sky and ghosts wept at night
events.text: A keeper of tales stares at the tracks of birds on the riverbank: every creature leaves its own sign. Could a sign stand for a thing, even when the thing is gone?

do.remember: saw that every track is a sign, and dreamed of signs for words

events.title: The Pillar of Heaven Shakes
events.text: The ground heaved and the sky seemed to tilt. The elders gather the children: it was like this when Gonggong broke Mount Buzhou.

tales.source: Han Feizi, Five Vermin; the bird and the sparks are from the later Shiyi Ji
tales.name: Suiren Drills Fire
tales.text: Long ago a wise one watched a bird peck at a tree until sparks flew. He took a stick and twirled it against dry wood until it smoked and caught. Since then the people have eaten cooked meat and no longer fear the dark.

tales.name: Nüwa Shapes the People
tales.text: The world was empty, and Nüwa was lonely. She knelt by the Yellow River and shaped people from its clay, one by one, until her hands were tired; then she dipped a rope in the mud and swung it, and every drop became a person.
tales.moral: all people are of one clay

tales.name: Nüwa Mends the Sky
tales.text: Gonggong, raging in defeat, struck his head against Mount Buzhou, the pillar of heaven. The sky cracked, fire and flood poured out. Nüwa melted stones of five colours to patch it, and cut the legs of a great turtle to hold the sky up again.
tales.moral: what is broken can be mended

tales.name: Shennong Tastes a Hundred Herbs
tales.text: Shennong wished to know which plants heal and which kill, so he tasted them all, a hundred in a day, and met seventy poisons. Each time he found the leaf that cured him. That is how the healers know what they know.

tales.name: Hou Yi Shoots the Suns
tales.text: When ten suns rose together and the rivers boiled, the archer Hou Yi drew his red bow and shot nine of them out of the sky. Nine golden crows fell to earth, and the one sun left has kept its place ever since.
tales.moral: courage can set the world right

tales.source: Shanhai Jing, Classic of the Northern Mountains
tales.name: Jingwei Fills the Sea
tales.text: The daughter of the Flame Emperor drowned in the eastern sea, and became the bird Jingwei. Every day she carries a pebble or a twig from the western hills and drops it into the sea. The sea laughs at her; she does not stop.

tales.source: Shanhai Jing, Classic of the Regions Beyond the North Seas
tales.name: Kuafu Chases the Sun
tales.text: The giant Kuafu raced the sun across the sky. He drank the Yellow River dry and the Wei River too, and still he thirsted; he died on the way to the great northern lake, and where his staff fell, a forest of peach trees grew.
tales.moral: know the limits of your strength
